title: Routine Spironolactone in Acute Myocardial Infarction
summary: In the companion CLEAR SYNERGY comparison, 7,062 post-PCI MI patients at 104 centers in 14 countries were randomized to routine spironolactone or placebo in a blinded 2-by-2 factorial trial. Cardiovascular death or new/worsening heart failure totaled 183 versus 220 events (1.7 vs 2.1 per 100 patient-years; competing-risk-adjusted HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.69–1.21; P=0.51), and the second coprimary composite occurred in 7.9% versus 8.3% (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.81–1.13; P=0.60). Serious adverse events occurred in 7.2% versus 6.8%.
findings: Total cardiovascular-death or new/worsening-HF events: 183 with spironolactone versus 220 with placebo, 1.7 versus 2.1 per 100 patient-years; adjusted HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.69–1.21), P=0.51.
Second coprimary outcome: 280/3,537 (7.9%) versus 294/3,525 (8.3%); adjusted HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.81–1.13), P=0.60.
population: Adults with acute myocardial infarction who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention at 104 centers in 14 countries.
limitations: The trial tested routine spironolactone in a broad post-PCI MI population, not specifically the high-risk subgroup with LVEF ≤40% plus heart-failure symptoms and/or diabetes for whom MRA therapy remains guideline-indicated. Its long-term outcomes are more relevant to inpatient/discharge planning than to an immediate ED intervention.
intervention: Spironolactone 25 mg once daily versus matching placebo, with independent colchicine/placebo allocation in the factorial design.
whyItMatters: Routine addition of spironolactone to a broad contemporary post-MI population did not improve the trial's coprimary outcomes. This argues against blanket MRA initiation after every MI, while leaving intact the established targeted indication for ACS patients with reduced LVEF plus heart-failure symptoms and/or diabetes.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. NEJM publisher metadata and PubMed verify online publication on 2024-11-17, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2405923, PMID 39555814, and free-article availability. The publisher abstract plus official trial-registry dosing metadata were reviewed; this record does not claim end-to-end full-text review. Targeted title/DOI checking found no correction or retraction. Later 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guidance retains a Class 1, LOE B-R MRA indication for ACS with LVEF ≤40% plus HF symptoms and/or diabetes, so CLEAR's neutral broad-population result is not presented as overturning that targeted indication.
primaryEndpoint: Two coprimary outcomes: total cardiovascular death or new/worsening heart-failure events; and first occurrence of MI, stroke, new/worsening heart failure, or cardiovascular death.
